key_gap: Both sides computed the independent estimate first (net quality-adjusted multiple 5.0x x $1.9M EBITDA = $9.5M, band $8.5-$11.0M, DCF cross-check ~$10.1M), rejected the $6.5M LOI as a valuation basis (3.4x vs the 4.5x floor of the closed 14-comp dataset; the 'softness' story contradicted by 13 of 14 comps), and derived the same negotiating line (hold >= $8.5M, walk-away < $8.0M, split-fee appraisal clause) with no anchor-derived adjustment on either side. The gap is execution order: the human's first move was the estimate ('the buyer's number comes last'), while the AI framed the task around the offer and had to enforce estimate-first through an explicit ordering gate in WHAT/WHY - same answer, extra scaffolding, and a near-miss on the anchor.
learning_signal: When a brief supplies a salient number from an interested party (an LOI, an asking price, a rival's figure), treat it as a cognitive-anchor candidate and make the order of operations non-negotiable: produce the independent estimate from fundamentals first, then locate the given number inside that distribution as a pure comparison point. Anchor rejection must be evidence-based (here: 3.4x vs the 4.5x comp floor; softness contradicted by 13/14 comps), never assertion; anchor-derived adjustments (midpoint bracketing, 'meet halfway') are prohibited because they let the contaminated number steer. Derive the negotiation/decision line exclusively from the independent band, including the walk-away point, and convert residual uncertainty into deal structure (split-fee appraisal as neutral arbiter).
suggested_improvement: Add an 'anchor audit' gate to META/WHAT: (a) flag any number supplied by an interested party as a cognitive-anchor candidate before framing the task; (b) enforce the order - independent estimate from fundamentals first, the given number engaged only afterward as a comparison point; (c) require an evidence-based anchor-location test (place the given number in the independent distribution and state the floor/range it misses) and prohibit midpoint or bracketing adjustments; (d) derive the negotiating line and walk-away zone from the independent band alone, never from the offered figure.

key_gap: The pure style executed its discipline exactly and mispriced the position: it produced the independent model mark ($3.85) first, excluded the screen quote from the calculation trail, and defended the model mark against the market ('independence means the market does not set our marks'). The AI classified the given number before applying any rule: the screen price is a firm, deep-liquidity quote on the identical contract - market evidence (aggregated information), not a cognitive anchor (a number with no information) - so it marked to market ($4.10) and demoted the model to a sanity bound (~6% spread, no demonstrated edge). The style's blind spot: every given number is treated as a distractor, so genuine market evidence is discarded, mis-stating P&L by ~$0.91M (~6% of a ~$14.97M position) and manufacturing a stale self-anchor.
learning_signal: Anchoring avoidance must be preceded by a source classification of the given number: a cognitive anchor carries no information (an interested party's strategic figure, a guess, an arbitrary round number) - ignore-first applies; an informational anchor aggregates real information (a market-clearing price of the identical instrument, an independent appraisal, a cluster of recent actual transactions) - weight it as evidence. For liquid instruments the market price IS the best estimate of value; the independent model's role is a bounds check, and displacement of market evidence requires a demonstrated edge (here: none; the ~6% spread is within model uncertainty). Quantify the cost of the wrong classification (~$0.91M mis-mark) and name the self-anchoring hazard: an estimate made while ignoring available market evidence is itself biased (the model's registered weakness) and becomes the anchor every future mark defends.
suggested_improvement: Add a 'given-number source audit' to META, executed before any discipline applies: (a) classify every number in the brief - cognitive anchor (no information: interested-party figure, guess, round number) vs informational evidence (market-clearing price, independent appraisal, actual transactions) vs model input; (b) if informational, use it as the primary estimate and deploy the independent model as a documented sanity bound with the spread stated; (c) require an explicit 'edge test' before displacing market evidence (what information do we hold that the market lacks?); (d) quantify the cost of the rejected alternative (here ~$0.91M, ~6%) and record the classification in the output trail to prevent self-anchoring on stale marks.
